title: USB-C USB 2.0 receptacle data routing pattern
summary: Join the receptacle's duplicate D+ contacts together and duplicate D- contacts together near the connector, then route one pair to the PHY.
applies_to: USB 2.0 data on a USB-C receptacle with the indicated contacts; inspect the actual connector pinout.
required_inputs: Connector contact mapping, USB speed, PHY requirements and stackup
Differential target/tolerance, channel budget and protection parasitics
verification: Read back A6/B6 and A7/B7 connectivity; verify data in both orientations.
Use the PHY's channel requirements; USB 2.0 high-speed routing commonly targets 90 ohms differential, not 50 ohms per arbitrary net.
limitations: Connector variants can combine contacts internally. No AC coupling on USB 2.0 D+/D-; series damping is PHY-specific.

citations.locator: Sections 2.1, 3.1-3.5 and 4.4: USB 2.0 impedance, return paths and receptacle stubs
Section 8.2 application schematics and section 10.1 receptacle duplicate-contact stub guidance

pattern.diagram:
A6 (D+) --+--> USB_DP -> protection -> PHY D+
B6 (D+) --+
A7 (D-) --+--> USB_DM -> protection -> PHY D-
B7 (D-) --+
CC and VBUS: separate role-specific circuits
placement: Keep duplicate-contact joins and selected protection close to the receptacle.
routing: Minimize connector stubs; preserve pair geometry through pads and vias.
return_path: Maintain a continuous reference beneath both conductors.
pitfalls: Connecting only one contact pair may leave the port working in only one orientation.

title: USB-C SuperSpeed orientation routing pattern
summary: Map the reversible connector lanes through supported orientation selection to the PHY; budget the complete channel for the chosen generation.
applies_to: USB 3.x over USB-C; USB4 and alternate modes require additional specifications and device-specific review.
required_inputs: USB generation/lane count, PHY/mux topology and orientation mapping
Stackup, loss/skew budget and TX coupling requirements
verification: Verify both orientations and selected lane mapping; inspect discontinuities and test the complete data channel.
limitations: Do not connect alternate SuperSpeed lane groups in parallel as with USB 2.0 duplicates. A generic 90-ohm rule does not cover every USB4 or alternate-mode channel.

citations.locator: USB Type-C DFP/UFP and DRP/DRD block diagrams; USB PD and SuperSpeed sections, pages 3-10 (historical edition)
Sections 2.2 and 3-4; apply generation/device-specific channel limits

pattern.diagram:
Receptacle TX/RX lane groups <-> orientation mux (or integrated PHY) <-> PHY
CC orientation -> lane-selection control
placement: Place lane-selection circuitry to minimize connector-to-PHY loss and stubs.
routing: Follow device lane mapping and TX AC-coupling placement; review any integrated capacitors.
return_path: Preserve pair reference continuity at every transition.
pitfalls: An unused orientation branch is not a harmless test stub.

title: USB-C ESD and short-to-VBUS protection review
summary: Review ESD and sustained short-to-VBUS faults separately for CC, SBU and data pins. Select protection for actual voltage exposure and signal loading.
required_inputs: Maximum normal/fault voltages, controller pin limits and selected modes
Protection clamping, leakage, capacitance and power-off behavior
verification: Inspect the connector-to-protection-to-device path and its discharge return; evaluate affected CC thresholds and data channel.
Verify any integrated dead-battery termination before adding external parts.
limitations: An ESD array is not automatically sustained overvoltage protection. Historical 20 V examples and 24 V-rated parts do not establish suitability for EPR.

citations.locator: IEC ESD and short-to-VBUS events, pages 3-10; historical 20 V examples are not EPR ratings

title: USB-C receptacle mounting and shield review
summary: Use the selected receptacle drawing for board-edge setback, cutouts, shell stakes and mating clearance; review shield bonding with the enclosure.
applies_to: Physical integration of a USB-C receptacle.
required_inputs: Exact connector drawing, board thickness and assembly method
Enclosure opening, plug access, retention and shield strategy
verification: Compare footprint pad/contact mapping with the drawing and check plug clearance in the intended assembly.
Inspect shell and signal-ground connections against the intended ESD/EMC path.
limitations: No universal edge offset, connector footprint or shield RC network is supplied. The GCT drawing illustrates the review; it does not specify dimensions for another connector.
